result:
Done. Both gates pass: `bun run typecheck` is clean and `bun test` shows 11 pass / 0 fail (the stack traces in the output are pre-existing logging from the `PostController` 422 test).

I added `app/Http/Support/redirect.ts`, a small guard module exporting `DEFAULT_REDIRECT` (`/dashboard`), `sanitizeRedirectPath(value)` — which strips control characters (browsers drop tabs/newlines while parsing URLs), trims, normalizes backslashes to slashes, and returns the value only if it is rooted at a single `/`, otherwise `null` — and `safeRedirectPath(value, fallback)`. `app/Http/Controllers/Auth/LoginController.ts` now runs both the validated body field and the `redirect` query-string fallback through that sanitizer in `store()`, so absolute URLs, protocol-relative `//host`, backslash variants and any non-path value fall back to `/dashboard` while `/posts/3/edit` still works; `show()` sanitizes the query value too, so the login form's hidden field can never carry an off-site target back to the server. Authentication logic itself is untouched — a wrong password still 422s without a session, and a correct one still signs in even when the redirect value is rejected. `tests/LoginController.test.ts` covers the sanitizer in isolation plus the end-to-end login flow for same-app, absolute, protocol-relative, backslash and query-string redirect values, the wrong-password case, and the sanitized page props (the filename also clears `guren check`'s missing-test warning for `LoginController`).
